newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks edge ahead to new record close.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks edge ahead to new record close.

text.p: Mexican stocks fended off a bout of profit-taking in late trade on Friday to advance slightly and notch up their third record-breaking close in a row on Friday.
"My read is there's lots of equity money flowing in from the States, as fears of a rates hike in the U.S. diminish," said Felix Boni, head of research at ING-Barings in Mexico.

Final closing prices situated the blue chip IPC share index was up 4.61 points on the day, or 0.11 percent, at 4,244.63. Heavy trading volume of 165.7 million shares traded confirmed heavy foreign investor interest.
Boni said mild U.S. producer prices data released before the bell encouraged the view increases in U.S. interest rates for the second half of 1997 would be restrained.
Many traders agreed market perception on U.S. interest rates was bullish.
"If you want to know what the market is thinking on interest rates, just look at the Dow Jones," said Ramon Ruiz, a sales trader at Latinvest in New York.
The Dow Jones industrial average advanced 70.57 points to its sixth record close in a row, at 7,782.04. U.S. 30-year Treasury bonds were up 18/32 to 6.73 percent.
The IPC had risen as high as 4,291.11 points in early trade, before profit-takers stepped into the market, dealers said.
"They were taking profits, I mean we've had a streak of record closes, so it was a good time to do so. The market still feels firm, though," a floor trader said. "Many stepped back in to buy low."
The trader said profit-taking was most evident in market heavyweight Telmex and glassmaker Vitro.
Telmex ended down 10 centavos at 18.90 pesos, but had earlier risen to a peso record of 19.24 pesos.

The telecomms stock's ADRs ended down 1/4 at 47-3/8, having declined from a year high of 48-3/8, a level not seen since the December 1994 devaluation crisis. Telmex ADRs reached a peak of more than 70 in February 1994.
Dealers drew attention to a strong performance by financial stocks, and several attributed this to speculation on a forthcoming government plan to restructure banks' past-due loans portfolios.
Bancomer, one of Mexico's largest financial groups, unseated Telmex from its customary first place on the most-traded stocks list .AV.MX.
Bancomer B, or common, shares gained 30 centavos to 3.70 pesos, while the preferred "A" shares ended up 9 centavos to 1.97 pesos.
Spanish-owned financial group BBV-Probursa gained 5 centavos at brisk trade to 2.06 pesos.
In percentage terms, financials also showed a dominant trend. The Abaco group gained 7 centavos to 81 centavos, while the Banacci group ended up 1.14 pesos at 21.00 pesos.
On the broad market, of 122 stocks traded, gainers outnumbered decliners by 59 to 37.

Dealers drew attention to broad-market gainer Corporacion Geo. The construction firm gained 1.80 pesos to 40.60 pesos on what dealers said were market expectations its June 17 primary share offering would be succesful.
(( --Martin Roberts, Mexico City newsroom +525 728-7907))
